passages.provision_quote: On receipt of a report of the existence of a homeless encampment, a city or town shall notify the owner to remove the owner's tent, structure or other personal property from the area in which the encampment is located. If removal does not occur within twenty-four hours after the order to remove the property, the city or town shall claim the property and retain the property for a period of fourteen days, during which the owner may claim the owner's property.
passages.note: The operative text requires notice and removal/disposal of property but states no civil or criminal penalty on the person for public-space camping itself.
Montenegro voted Y on final House passage of this single-subject homeless-encampment-removal bill.

rows.reasoning: Montenegro voted Y on final House passage of SB 1413 (2023), a single-subject homeless-encampment-removal bill, in-term. Its operative section only orders notice and removal/disposal of property within 24 hours, with no civil or criminal penalty on the person for public-space camping itself -- the annex's 'clearances and sweeps with notice but no penalty on the person' hard case for rung 4 ('Prohibiting encampments on public property, enforced through graduated warnings and civil penalties'), so the penalty clause is unevidenced.
